accuracy.evidence: Grounded in the EEF guidance report on metacognition and self-regulated learning (plan, monitor, evaluate, and explicit teaching of strategies) and Dunlosky et al. (2013), which rated practice testing and distributed practice as high utility and re-reading and highlighting as low. The week results are explicitly labelled as example figures, and the pattern they show (re-reading feels strong but retains least) matches Roediger and Karpicke (2006).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the belief that feeling sure means you know it (the week bars put felt-sure next to the Friday score, and Ali's quiz story), choosing a method because it is quick, fun or neat (weak reason options and the fun tag), cramming in one session (plan 2 and the cram tag), keeping a failed method or quitting the task instead of switching (Keep on a low check is refused, quit tag), and that slow means it failed (Mia's diagram).

lab_distinct.evidence: The flagstrat lab combines a task card dropped onto a two-by-two grid of study tools, a week planner where each revision plan lights its study days and grows paired felt-sure and score bars, a two-slot I'll-because sentence builder, a feeling-versus-proof verdict on short stories, and a try-check-switch loop with a goal line on a score bar. None of these mechanics appear in the reflection or retrieval labs, and the shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Steps follow the plan-do-evaluate cycle in order: know which tool suits which kind of task, see with data why felt confidence misleads, state a plan with a task-based reason before starting, judge outcomes on evidence, then put it all together by trying, checking against a goal and switching when the check fails. Each completion line names the rule, such as that switching after a poor check is smart, not giving up.

predictions.evidence: Three committed predictions come before the evidence: reading the spelling list again versus covering and testing (re-reading is the popular choice), which week plan will score best (tempting re-reading five times, because it feels thorough), and whether Ali's strategy worked when he felt very sure (tempting yes). Each reveal is compared with the bars or the quiz score the learner then sees.

challenge_feedback.evidence: The five-question challenge has a specific reply for each wrong choice: poster and re-read options explain why testing makes facts stick, give up is redirected to switching, fun and just-start options explain what a good reason contains, felt-easy and took-ages options explain why neither is proof, and cram and no-difference options explain spacing. Correct answers name both skills, choosing with a reason and judging on proof.

readability.evidence: Learner paragraphs use short sentences and define strategy, proof and switching in plain words, within the learner kid target; the adult text introduces retrieval practice, spaced practice, elaboration, dual coding and the illusion of fluency with one-line glosses inside the adult target. Lab prompts are one short instruction each, and every plan sentence is shown in full once built.

no_filler.evidence: The key idea lists the four tool-task pairs and the judge-on-proof rule in two sentences; the family tip gives two exact questions and a two-minute fallback; the adult notes spend their space on the evidence base, exact terms, common mistakes and a caution about praise. Numeric items count marks short of a goal, minutes of spaced practice or score gains rather than unrelated sums.

mobile.evidence: Checked on an iPhone 13 viewport in both themes and on desktop: all six steps render, five tasks complete through Show me and the challenge appears. Phone screenshots caught three problems that were fixed before commit: strategy rows showing only their first letter, the week box overlapping plan 3, and the tallest bar label touching the legend. Rows are full width and at least 50 pixels tall.

accessibility.evidence: axe reported no violations in light or dark theme on desktop or phone. Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: four tool buttons, run-plan buttons naming each plan, strategy and reason buttons, verdict buttons with the full verdict as their accessible name, and Keep and Switch buttons. The canvas aria-label tracks each status message, and challenge feedback is in a polite live region.
